html:
The Empire of Alexander was the realm that Alexander the Great of Macedon won in about eleven years of war, stretching from Greece and Egypt to the Indus. It is shown here as it was at his death in Babylon in 323 BCE.

Alexander inherited Macedon and command over the Greeks from his father Philip II in 336 BCE. In his conquests he crossed into Asia in 334, beat the Persian king Darius III at Issus and at the Battle of Gaugamela, and took over the whole Achaemenid Empire. He pushed on through Central Asia to India, where his army refused to go further.

He mostly kept the Persian system of provinces, often with Persian governors, and founded many cities, the greatest being Alexandria in Egypt. When he died at 32 with no adult heir, his generals divided the provinces among themselves in the Partition of Babylon. Their wars of succession broke the empire into kingdoms such as the Kingdom of Antigonus, the Seleucids and the Ptolemies.
